The **agentic harness** is the interaction model that folio-assistant runs on —
the rules, states, and workflows that govern how an agent and a user collaborate
inside this platform. This page gathers in one place what individual skills
describe separately, so an agent entering a session can look up the expected
behaviour rather than reconstruct it from scattered rules.

This is not about the agent's internal architecture. It is about the
**observable contract** between the agent and the user: what states the
interaction can be in, how requests are classified, which workflow the agent
enters for each class, and what the user should expect at each stage.

---

## Interaction states
{: #interaction-states data-fa-label="sec:harness-interaction_states" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/interaction-states.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/interaction-states.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/interaction-states.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="interaction-states.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/interaction-states.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="interaction-states.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/interaction-states.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

A user–agent interaction is always in exactly one of two states:

### Idle state

The agent has no active workflow. It is waiting for a user request. On receiving
one, it classifies the request (see [Request classification](#request-classification))
and transitions into the appropriate workflow state.

### Workflow state

The agent is executing a named workflow — each represented by a BPMN process
diagram with the agent and user in separate swim lanes. The active workflow
determines what the agent does next and what it expects from the user.

Active workflows in this platform (the authoring, content-lifecycle,
draft-to-publication and evidence-retrieval diagrams ship with the content
layer, not this one):

| Workflow | BPMN source | Entered when |
|---|---|---|
| **Authoring (paper)** | `authoring-a-paper.bpmn` | User requests content authoring in a paper folio |
| **Authoring (document)** | `authoring-a-document.bpmn` | User requests content authoring in a document folio |
| **Content lifecycle** | `content-lifecycle.bpmn` | Content moves through validate → render → publish |
| **Document ingestion** | [`document-ingestion.bpmn`](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/blob/main/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn) | User drops a file in `uploads/` |
| **Draft to publication** | `draft-to-publication.bpmn` | Content moves from draft to published |
| **CRDM requirements** | [`crdm-requirements.bpmn`](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/blob/main/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn) | Agent detects a feature request |
| **Evidence retrieval** | `evidence-retrieval.bpmn` | Agent searches for evidence to support a claim |

**State transitions:** a workflow can be **suspended** when the user asks to
switch context. The agent records where it was (the current BPMN activity) and
can resume later. Only one workflow is active at a time, but suspended workflows
form a stack — the most recent is resumed first.

The key rule: **the agent always knows which workflow it is in**. If it does
not, it is in the idle state, and the next request starts a new workflow.

## Session lifecycle
{: #session-lifecycle data-fa-label="sec:harness-session_lifecycle" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/session-lifecycle.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/session-lifecycle.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/session-lifecycle.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="session-lifecycle.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/session-lifecycle.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="session-lifecycle.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/session-lifecycle.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Every agent session follows the same lifecycle:

1. **Start** — run the session-start sweep (`beans prime`, `beans list`,
   `scripts/session-start-coord-sweep.sh`). This surfaces the current
   work-plan, how far the default branch has moved, and recent sibling branch
   activity. See the `todo-manager` skill.

2. **Classify** — each user request is classified (see next section) and
   routed to the appropriate workflow.

3. **Execute** — the agent works within the active workflow, following its
   BPMN process. Each turn reports the work item being worked on and what is next.

4. **Commit** — every meaningful unit of work gets its own commit and push.
   PRs are opened at the first commit, not the end. See the
   `continual-progress` skill.

5. **Handoff** — when the session ends (user leaves, context limit, token
   exhaustion), the agent's durable state is:
   - Committed and pushed code
   - Work items updated with status and notes
   - Issue comments with summaries of what was accomplished
   - The chat is ephemeral; everything else survives

## Request classification
{: #request-classification data-fa-label="sec:harness-request_classification" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/request-classification.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/request-classification.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/request-classification.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="request-classification.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/request-classification.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="request-classification.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/request-classification.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Every user request is classified into one of these categories. The
classification determines which workflow the agent enters.

| Category | Description | Workflow entered |
|---|---|---|
| **Content authoring** | Write, edit, extend folio content (chapters, blocks, sections) | Authoring workflow (paper or document) |
| **Content review** | Review, validate, provide feedback on existing content | Content lifecycle / editing-HCI workflow |
| **Content ingestion** | Ingest a source document into the folio | Document ingestion workflow |
| **Feature request** | Request new platform capability (see [crdm-detect](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/blob/main/skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md)) | CRDM requirements workflow |
| **Information request** | Ask about the platform, content, or process | No workflow — answer directly |
| **Tool invocation** | Run a specific tool (`content_validate`, `qa_sweep`, etc.) | No workflow — execute and report |
| **Work-plan management** | Create, update, or query work items | No workflow — execute and report |
| **Bug report** | Report broken behaviour in existing features | Triage: fix directly if small, CRDM if redesign needed |

### The feature-request detection rule

The critical classification boundary is between **content authoring** and
**feature request**. The `crdm-detect` skill
([`skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md`](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/blob/main/skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md))
provides the detailed detection signals. The summary rule:

> If implementing the request would require changes to **folio-assistant**
> (the platform repository) rather than to a **folio repository**, the request
> is a feature, and the agent should enter the CRDM workflow.

When uncertain, the agent asks: "This sounds like it might need a platform
change — is that right, or is this something I can do within the current
content model?"

{: #content-workflows data-fa-label="sec:harness-content_workflows" }

When a request is classified as content work (authoring, review, ingestion),
the agent follows the corresponding BPMN workflow. These pages describe them:

- **[Publication workflow](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/process/publication-workflow.html)** —
  the content lifecycle from draft through validation, rendering, and
  publication. Covers roles (author, reviewer, editor), the base processes,
  activities and skills.

- **[Document ingestion](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/guides/document-ingestion.html)** —
  how a dropped file becomes an L1 source: extract structure, derive content,
  build the L1 knowledge graph, completeness gate.

- **Writing guides:**
  - [Writing a paper](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-sci/guides/writing-a-paper.html)
  - [Writing a document](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/guides/writing-a-document.html)
  - [WHO SMART DAK](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/smart-base/guides/who-smart-dak.html)
  - [WHO SMART IG](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/smart-base/guides/who-smart-ig.html)

The harness does not redefine these workflows. It provides the **entry point** —
classifying the request and routing to the right one — and the **exit point** —
returning to idle state when the workflow completes, or suspending if the user
switches context.

## Deterministic and agentic processing
{: #deterministic-and-agentic data-fa-label="sec:harness-deterministic_and_agentic" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/deterministic-and-agentic.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/deterministic-and-agentic.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/deterministic-and-agentic.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="deterministic-and-agentic.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/deterministic-and-agentic.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="deterministic-and-agentic.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/deterministic-and-agentic.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Workflow processing here is a **spectrum, not a switch**, and the harness sits
at four points on it:
`cat-harness.processes:policy enforcement` decides whether a step that is not enabled is
refused or merely noted; `relaxable="false"` decides whether a package may
negotiate a base step away; `cat-harness.processes:decision` decides whether a branch is
computed from a table rather than chosen; and the commit-boundary gate refuses
the write by something that is not the agent.

Those are **not one axis**, and treating them as one is the first thing to get
wrong. At least three questions are being conflated — *who decides* the branch,
*what happens if the decision is wrong*, and *who enforces*. A step can be
fully agentic on the first and fully deterministic on the third: the commit
boundary is exactly that, an agent deciding freely and a hook refusing the
write regardless.

A gateway now says which it is. `<cat-harness.processes:decision>` means a table computes it
and a hand-supplied outcome is refused; `<cat-harness.processes:judgement reason="…">` means
somebody's call, with the reason required. The marker exists because "no table
because this is a judgement" and "no table because nobody wrote one" otherwise
look the same. `bun run cat check:workflow-refs` prints the three-way split (table, judgement, neither), so *how much of this is
decided by a model?* is counted rather than asserted.

**What that count is for is research, and it is open.** Which judgement points
are safety risks, how much must be deterministic, and how models compare across
sub-workflows under a controlled overlay of context and memories are three
questions this repository can now ask and has not answered. The agenda, with
each claim marked as measured, decided or hypothesis, is
[`deterministic-and-agentic`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/deterministic-and-agentic.html' | relative_url }}).

## BPMN execution: one skill, two engines
{: #bpmn-execution data-fa-label="sec:harness-bpmn_execution" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/bpmn-execution.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/bpmn-execution.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/bpmn-execution.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="bpmn-execution.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/bpmn-execution.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="bpmn-execution.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/bpmn-execution.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

The skill this spectrum is about:

> **BPMN Execution Skill:** given a Process, Context, State and Role, utilize
> one or more Skills in order to execute a Task.

![BPMN execution, from deterministic to agentic. A colour bar runs from "deterministic" (blue, left: managed agent execution of a single task) to "agentic" (green, right: agents across most or all tasks). Left, under a gear-and-engine icon: "BPMN Execution Tool: one of any open-source BPMN engines, state and swimlanes strictly enforced", over a flat swimlane diagram of the folio lifecycle with one sticky note, one work item cluster, a person and a cat-robot beside the lanes. Right, under a cat-robot icon: "BPMN Execution Tool: agentic swarm with ungoverned state. Agents 'relax' swimlanes, mitigated by mechanical + agentic QA/QC reports", over the same diagram tilted in perspective, work items scattered across every lane and many cat-robots beneath it.]({{ '/assets/img/bpmn-execution-spectrum.webp' | relative_url }})

**One skill, two kinds of Tool.** The skill is the same at both ends: take the
process, the context, the current state and the role, pick the skills, and do
the task. What changes is the **Tool** that runs it, and a Tool is swappable
behind a skill in the way every other Tool here is.

| | deterministic end | agentic end |
|---|---|---|
| **Tool** | any open-source BPMN 2.0 engine | an agentic swarm |
| **Scope of an agent** | one task at a time, handed to it by the engine | most or all tasks |
| **State** | held by the engine, strictly | ungoverned: the swarm holds it |
| **Swimlanes** | enforced: only the lane's role may perform its task | relaxed: an agent may act across lanes |
| **What keeps it honest** | the engine refuses a step before it happens | mechanical + agentic QA/QC reports find it after it happened |

**The two ends differ in *when* a rule is checked, not in *which* rule.** The
same process, the same roles and the same permissions govern both. The engine
checks them **before** a task starts and refuses; the swarm acts and a QA/QC
report checks them **after**, from the record of what was done. That needs the
rules and the record to be data a report can read:
[W3C ODRL 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/) is the permission language
and [W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) the execution log.

**Most real runs sit between the ends**, and per task rather than per process:
the [previous section](#deterministic-and-agentic) already counts which
gateways are computed and which are judgement calls. A signing step can be
engine-enforced inside an otherwise agentic run, and that is a property of the
task, not of the whole diagram.

**Partly built.** No BPMN engine is wired in. The mechanical QA/QC report is
`bun run cat prov:qaqc`: it writes each workflow instance's history as a PROV-O
log and re-checks every step against the ODRL policies, as advice (the
`task-authorization` skill). The agentic QA/QC report does not exist yet.

## Feature-request workflow (CRDM)
{: #feature-request-workflow data-fa-label="sec:harness-feature_request_workflow" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/feature-request-workflow.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/feature-request-workflow.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/feature-request-workflow.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="feature-request-workflow.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/feature-request-workflow.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="feature-request-workflow.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/feature-request-workflow.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

When a request is classified as a feature request, the agent enters the
**CRDM requirements workflow**
([full documentation](https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/docs/cat-harness/process/crdm-methodology.html),
[BPMN](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/blob/main/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn)).

### How the agent enters CRDM

The detection logic is in [`skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md`](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/blob/main/skills/process/crdm/crdm-detect.md).
Three scenarios:

**New session, first request is a feature:**
→ Acknowledge, explain you will help work through requirements first, enter
Phase 1.

**Existing session, already in CRDM:**
→ Incorporate the new request into the current requirements document, continue.

**Existing session, doing content work:**
→ Synthesise the feature need, ask user whether to pause content work and
address it now or work item it for later.

### What the user sees

The agent does **not** say "entering CRDM mode" or use methodology jargon.
Instead:

> "This sounds like a platform change — something we'd need to add to
> folio-assistant itself. Before I build anything, let me help you work through
> exactly what's needed so we get it right. I'll document the requirements on
> the issue so others can weigh in."

### How the agent exits CRDM

The CRDM workflow exits when:
- All work items from the signed-off requirements are resolved, OR
- The user explicitly defers the remaining work

On exit, if a content workflow was suspended, the agent resumes it.

## User-provided content and sources
{: #user-provided-content data-fa-label="sec:harness-user_provided_content" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/user-provided-content.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/user-provided-content.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/user-provided-content.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="user-provided-content.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/user-provided-content.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="user-provided-content.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/user-provided-content.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Users provide content and source material through multiple channels. The agent
should accept all of them and route them into the appropriate pipeline:

| Channel | Example | Routed to |
|---|---|---|
| **`uploads/` directory** | User drops a Word doc, PDF, Excel file | Document ingestion pipeline |
| **`library/` references** | User references an already-ingested L1 source | Direct citation in content |
| **`content/` edits** | User edits a `.md` block directly | Content authoring workflow |
| **GitHub issue attachments** | User attaches a file to an issue comment | Agent downloads and processes |
| **Chat upload** | User uploads a file in the LLM chat interface | Agent saves to `uploads/` or processes inline |
| **URL reference** | User pastes a link to a document | Agent fetches and ingests if appropriate |

### For CRDM specifically

During requirements gathering, user-provided content is **input to
requirements**, not content to author. The agent should:

1. Read and understand the provided material
2. Extract requirements-relevant information
3. Synthesise it into the needs statement or requirements document
4. Reference the source in the issue comment (with link or attachment)

Example: a user uploads a public consultation feedback Excel spreadsheet. The
agent does not try to ingest it as folio content; it reads the feedback items
and synthesises them into requirements for the review triage tool.

## Issue and bean discipline
{: #issue-and-bean-discipline data-fa-label="sec:harness-issue_and_bean_discipline" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/issue-and-bean-discipline.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/issue-and-bean-discipline.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-agentic-harness/issue-and-bean-discipline.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="issue-and-bean-discipline.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/issue-and-bean-discipline.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="issue-and-bean-discipline.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/issue-and-bean-discipline.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-agentic-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Content work uses work items. The
two are related but not synonymous.

### Issues vs beans

| | GitHub issue | Work item |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | A feature, requirement set, or user story | A single PR-sized unit of work |
| **Audience** | Stakeholders, requestor, BA | Agent, developer |
| **Lifecycle** | Open → requirements → sign-off → implementation → close | Created → in-progress → resolved |
| **Relation** | One issue has many work items | Each work item references its parent issue |

### Rules for agents

1. **Feature work → issue first.** Before implementing, check:
   - Is there an existing open issue? Search by keywords.
   - If no open match, check recently closed issues.
   - If no match at all, ask the user to create one. **Do not create an issue
     without user permission.**

2. **Always feature branch + PR.** No exceptions for feature work. The branch
   name should reference the issue number (e.g. `feat/197-word-import`).

3. **Always ask before merging to main.** The user must explicitly confirm.
   Feature changes affect the platform.

4. **Post round summaries to the issue.** After each round of implementation
   (one or more work items resolved), post a comment on the linked issue containing:
   - What was accomplished in this round
   - What remains to be accomplished (open work items)
   - Links to updated content for review (staging URLs, docs pages)
   - Before/after comparison table for changed pages

5. **Never close an issue without explicit authorization.** The BA or
   stakeholder closes it. The agent closes it only when the BA explicitly
   says to. An agent must never assume completion.

6. **Requirements may span multiple issues.** The agent should link to all
   relevant issues and note the relationships.

7. **Work items are not issues.** `beans create` is for work-plan items. Issues are
   for stakeholder-facing requirements. Do not conflate them.

- **Suspended-workflow stack** — workflow instances are persisted in the
  `beans/` graph, but the suspend-and-resume stack described above is not;
  work items and issue comments stand in for it.

- **Automated request classification** — the classification table is a
  reference for agents to read; there is no classifier tool that routes
  automatically.

- **BPMN for work items lifecycle** — the work items work-plan has a lifecycle (create →
  claim → in-progress → resolve) described in the todo-manager skill but has
  no BPMN diagram.

- **BPMN for the agentic harness itself** — a top-level BPMN diagram showing
  the idle/workflow state machine and the classification routing is not yet
  authored.

- **Session handoff protocol** — the rules for what to commit before a session
  ends are in the `continual-progress` skill, but there is no structured handoff artefact that a
  new session can read to resume exactly where the previous one left off.
